messages:
arjun: quick heads-up — i brought up the new 'sable-mini-compact' embed on staging and ran the default multilingual holdout. overall recall looks OK but french subset collapsed.
claire: can you paste the exact eval command and the dataset split you used?
arjun: `python eval/recall.py --model sable-mini-compact --holdout multilingual --k 5 --seed 42`
        dataset: multilingual-holdout-v2 (en,fr,es,de)
        overall: R@1=0.783, R@5=0.928
        en: R@1=0.812
        fr: R@1=0.612  <-- big delta
        es: R@1=0.765
matt: hmm. did you use the same tokenizer & normalization pipeline as baseline? any truncation/profile differences?
dar: also which quant profile? int4/int8/float16?
arjun: quant profile: `int4-fast32` (local ONNX route). i re-ran float16 as a quick check: float16 fr R@1=0.79 (so float16 matches baseline). so this looks quant-specific and language-skewed.
claire: silhouette / cluster purity numbers?
arjun: ran kmeans 100 clusters on holdout embeddings:
        silhouette_en=0.45, silhouette_fr=0.12, silhouette_es=0.39
        per-cluster top-domain frequency shows fr docs split across many small clusters.
embed-ci-bot: CI: run 3467894321-1 holdout/multilang/recall completed. Regression detector: FR R@1 delta -0.17 vs baseline :warning:
matt: could be quantization sensitivity for francophone tokens — maybe subword distribution or avg token lengths differ. try disabling per-token clamp or using symmetric quant in the int4 path.
dar: also check L2 norms pre/post-quant. int4 can skew magnitudes and break cosine.
arjun: good call — quick L2 stats:
        float16 mean_norm_fr=7.02 std=1.12
        int4 mean_norm_fr=5.11 std=1.85
        float16 mean_norm_en=7.08 std=1.09
        int4 mean_norm_en=6.95 std=1.22
        -> FR norm collapsed and variance increased under int4.
claire: that explains cos similarity drop. sample-nearest neighbors for a few failing FR queries? paste top3 ids.
arjun: sample qid=23456 expected=9876 top3(int4)=[10234, 5561, 9876]
        float16 top3=[9876, 10234, 5561]
matt: order flip shows margin is small but quant noise pushed canonical match down. can we try per-language rescaling / per-channel quant stats?
dar: yes run per-channel calibration (`--quant-calib per_channel`) and a small re-eval. also try symmetric vs asymmetric scheme.
arjun: firing tests now: per_channel + symmetric int4, and an int4 fallback policy that uses float16 for queries detected as non-en (langid>0.7 fr) — naive but quick.
embed-ci-bot: CI: queued 3467894321-2 (per_channel int4) and 3467894321-3 (int4+lang-fallback). i'll post results.
claire: if per-channel fixes it, we should add a multilingual quant smoke to the onboarding checklist. 
matt: agree — action item: add test(holdout multilingual small, check norm drift, per-lang recall delta) to embed onboarding checklist.
dar: and add probe: compute top-1 reorder rate between baseline float16 and quantized to detect fragile queries.
arjun: noted. i'll update the onboarding doc and follow up with numbers when CI returns. if it still fails, we'll pin sable-mini-compact to float16 for now for non-en customers.
claire: thanks — informative thread. :thumbsup:
arjun: will post final numbers when runs finish.
embed-ci-bot: CI: run 3467894321-2 completed. per_channel int4 FR R@1=0.73 (improved) ; run 3467894321-3 completed. int4+lang-fallback FR R@1=0.78 (matches float16) :white_check_mark:
